item.title: INEC, security agencies addressing security concerns ahead of 2027 polls – Amupitan
item.description: Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Joash Amupitan, says the commission, in collaboration with security agencies, is taking necessary steps to address all security concerns ahead of the 2027 general elections. Amupitan ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍⁠​⁠‌‌‍‍‌‌​stated this on Saturday in Jos while speaking with newsmen during the monitoring of the ongoing mock accreditation. Addressing a question on the security challenge and the likely implications on voter participation, Amupitan said the safety of ad hoc staff and all Nigerians remained a priority to the commission. “As the chairman of INEC, I’m also worried about the state of security in Nigeria, but you can see we are taking some good steps to ensure that we nip it in the bud. “Just two days ago, we had a national security conference where we brought together all the members of the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security (ICCES), the police, the military, the Civil Defence, and other paramilitary agencies. “So, we had a one-day conference where we discussed all these issues,” he said. Amupitan said that INEC had conducted a risk assessment of every part of Nigeria, using Election Risk Management (ERM) tools. “We have identified all the polling units that are vulnerable, and we have shared this with the law enforcement agencies so that they can make extraordinary preparation for those places. “Any polling unit 500 meters from those vulnerable areas has been identified, and we are going to deal with it,” he said. Amupitan said the commission was interested in the security of the voters and ad hoc staff, particularly corps members. “It’s not every security matter you can bring to the open, but we are doing everything, both intelligence and physical, to ensure that the security on election day is assured,” he said. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the monitoring of the mock accreditation exercise was still ongoing in different parts of the state as of the time of filling this report. (NAN) The post INEC, security agencies addressing security concerns ahead of 2027 polls – Amupitan appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Electricity’ll improve, Mbah and I are working on Eastern Gas Pipeline – Tinubu
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has said electricity supply will improve in the South-East, adding that his administration has approved the Eastern Gas Pipeline and Eastern Nigeria rail line as part of plans to boost infrastructure and connectivity in the region. Tinubu made the remarks on Saturday during the All Progressives Congress presidential campaign rally in Enugu, where he said he was working with Enugu State Governor Peter Mbah on the gas pipeline project. “Electricity will improve. The Eastern Gas Pipeline is approved. Peter Mbah and I are working on it,” the president said. He also announced the approval of the Eastern Nigeria rail line, saying the projects would improve connections between the South-East, South-South and northern parts of the country. “Also approved is the Eastern Nigeria rail line. We will connect you, connect the East, South and North. It’s our honest promise for development,” he said. Addressing farmers in the region, Tinubu promised interest-free loans and financial support, alongside measures to reduce the challenges associated with farming. “To our farmers, they will receive money, loans that are interest-free. We will relieve them of the burdens of farming. We will connect with infrastructure,” he said. The president also urged residents to participate in the January 16 election, asking them to collect their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) and turn out to vote for the APC. “January 16, you must go out and vote. Take your friends, take your brothers, take your sisters. You must collect your PVC and go there, for President, vote APC, for honourable, APC,” Tinubu said. item.title: Referee faces suspension after punching goalkeeper in post-match rawl
item.description: A Bolivian referee, Jordy Aleman, might face be faced with strict suspension rules after punching Real Potosi goalkeeper Cristian Martinez during a post-match confrontation following the 2026 Copa Bolivia final. The incident occurred on Wednesday after Always Ready secured the trophy with a 3-1 aggregate victory over Real Potosi. The second leg ended in a goalless draw at the Victor Agustin Ugarte Stadium in Potosi. Tensions flared after the final whistle as Real Potosi players approached Aleman to protest decisions made during the match. Television footage showed the referee punching Martinez in the face, triggering further disorder before police intervened to protect the officials. Reports from Spanish-language media, including MARCA, said the confrontation followed an insult directed at Aleman by the goalkeeper. Martinez reportedly told the referee, “I hope your mother dies.” Martinez later said the punch left his mouth bleeding. However, in a defiant response reported by El Diario, he remarked: “He should hit harder.” The goalkeeper also questioned Aleman’s professionalism and called for an exemplary punishment. He subsequently announced that he would not pursue legal action or file a formal complaint over the incident. In a statement shared by Spanish publication 20 Minutos, Martinez said: “My intention is to consider this episode over and avoid allowing this situation to continue generating conflict.” Aleman could face disciplinary sanctions under the Bolivian Football Federation’s Disciplinary Code, which reportedly provides for fines of at least 20 national minimum monthly salaries and bans of between one and three years for physical assaults. The incident also led to four Real Potosi players and three members of the club’s coaching staff reportedly receiving red cards. According to Bolivian publication Vision 360, the federation’s refereeing authorities are expected to review the incident alongside the match reports. Aleman’s status as an international referee could also have further implications. The referee has yet to make a public statement on the incident. item.title: Meet Nigerian’s Maria Wophill named World Athletics’ Woman of the Year
item.description: Veteran Nigerian sports administrator Maria Wophill has been named the World Athletics (WA) 2026 Woman of the Year in recognition of her decades-long contribution to gender equality and the development of women and girls in athletics. World Athletics announced the honour as part of its 2026 awards, recognising Wophill’s efforts to create opportunities for women in track and field through leadership, advocacy and grassroots development. Wophill previously served as secretary-general of the Athletics Federation of Nigeria (AFN) between 2005 and 2013. She has also held senior positions in the Federal Ministry of Youth and Sports Development and served on the World Athletics Women’s Committee from 2010 to 2018. Her contributions to Nigerian sports administration include advocacy for increased female representation on the boards of national sports federations, which helped secure additional positions for women. At the continental level, she championed the establishment of the Confederation of African Athletics (CAA) Gender Leadership Task Force in 2024. She has also mentored female coaches and sports administrators through the Women’s Sport Leadership Academy (WISH), while supporting grassroots participation through the Abuja FCT Girls Sprints and Relays, an initiative aimed at encouraging secondary school girls to take part in athletics. Reacting to the recognition, Wophill expressed gratitude to World Athletics and Nigerian sports organisations, describing the award as a motivation to continue contributing to the sport. “This has been a truly humbling year and I am very proud to be acknowledged for the work I have done,” she said. She added that the recognition had strengthened her commitment to promoting gender leadership, safeguarding young athletes and mentoring people within athletics. “This award has energised me to keep giving my best in all positions in athletics, with particular focus on gender leadership, safeguarding young athletes and mentoring within the sport,” she said. World Athletics President Sebastian Coe described Wophill as a deserving recipient, praising her efforts to improve female representation and mentor others in the sport. Her recognition is part of the 2026 World Athletics Awards, with the World Athletes of the Year, Rising Stars and Moment of the Year scheduled to be announced on Sunday. item.title: [PHOTOS] Moment Voter Makes Frustrating Facial Expressions While Being Captured On INEC’s BVAS
item.description: A voter at polling unit 001 in Barnawa, Kaduna South Local Government Area, captured attention on Saturday, as she made different frustrating facial expressions while being captured on the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) during the INEC’s mock accreditation exercise in Kaduna State. Our correspondent, who monitored the exercise, noted that a voter spent more than five minutes completing the accreditation and voting process due to network challenges affecting the machine. The exercise is expected to simulate the Presidential election, with polling units opening by 8:30 a.m. and accreditation running from 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. Meanwhile, one of the voters at polling unit 002, Narayi Primary School, in Kaduna State, Rebecca Oladipo, has expressed frustration over the absence of the Independent National Electoral Commission’s officials at the mock accreditation on Saturday. Oladipo, who said she arrived at the polling unit for the INEC mock accreditation exercise at 10:30 am, questioned the commission’s preparedness to conduct a credible election in 2027, expressing concern that the mock election, which is expected to test INEC’s operational readiness, appears to be starting on a shaky note. According to her, the delay left those who turned up for the exercise waiting without knowing when the exercise would commence. Rebecca Oladipo “I’m here at Narayi Primary School, one of the wards chosen for the mock exercise. I have been here for the past two hours. INEC is supposed to start the exercise at 8:30. Now we are at around 10:30, and we are yet to see them. “This is really disheartening because a lot of people have been here. Security agencies have been here; even I came to meet them here. One or two voters have been here, and they left. “I’m using this opportunity to say to INEC that we in Narayi ward are not happy because we heard that other wards have started the exercises, so we should not be left behind. “I’m using this opportunity to tell INEC that in the main election, please, please, let it not be like this. It has always been like this in the previous elections. Maybe because Narayi people are good and kind people. They are quiet people. “But please, I hope that everyone knows that the 2027 general election is a critical one. So, we are begging that they should make everything available. “Whatever may make them come late during the 2027 election, they should please avoid it.” The mock exercise, expected to simulate the Presidential election, is expected to open by 8:30 a.m., and accreditation will run from 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. The post [PHOTOS] Moment Voter Makes Frustrating Facial Expressions While Being Captured On INEC’s BVAS appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Low turnout, BVAS glitches mar INEC mock accreditation in Ondo
item.description: By Dayo Johnson Akure The ongoing mock accreditation and voting exercise conducted by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) ahead of the 2027 general elections has recorded low voter turnout in some polling units in Ondo State, alongside technical challenges with the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS). As of the time of filing this report, findings showed that only two persons voted out of 470 registered voters at Tipper Garage, Ward 2, Unit 046. Similarly, at Champion Junction, Ward 3, Unit 15, only six voters participated in the exercise. At High Court, Ward 5, Unit 11, 11 persons were recorded as having voted out of 940 registered voters. However, the situation was different at Ajipowo, Ward 2, Unit 17, where a large turnout of voters was observed. Despite the turnout, the exercise experienced technical challenges as the BVAS reportedly failed to capture the faces of some elderly voters, causing difficulties during the accreditation process. The mock exercise is part of INEC’s preparations to test its electoral equipment and processes ahead of the 2027 general elections. item.title: Why Tinubu should stay in office for 10 years – Akande
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde Former Osun State Governor, Bisi Akande, has called for President Bola Tinubu to remain in office for 10 years, saying the period would allow him to complete ongoing projects and deliver lasting reforms. Akande made the call during an interview on the Frankly Speaking with Icon podcast, published on Friday. “He should remain in office, if possible, for another 10 years; otherwise, we go back to the situation of ‘Ebinpawa’ because there has been a foundation for hunger,” Akande said. He cited the Olubadan’s comments on road projects across the South-West, including routes linking Ijebu-Ode, Abeokuta, Oyo and Ikire, as evidence of the administration’s ongoing work. Quoting the traditional ruler, Akande said: “If you are working like this, and this had not been done 50 years before you, what again do we still say you should do, and you have not done? “But so that you will be able to complete this good job that you started, Ibadan people and Oyo State people are supporting you to do another four years.” Akande also blamed successive military administrations for what he described as decades of neglect of agriculture, education and economic development, saying their policies contributed to the country’s present difficulties. “Forty years before he came, since 1966, when the military started ruling you, you have been laying the foundation for hunger. You have abandoned your farms. You have abandoned the job. You have refused to be educated. You have refused to be modernised,” he said. He expressed optimism that Tinubu’s policies would produce significant improvements in the coming years, particularly in electricity supply and modernisation. “So in another 10 years there will be electricity everywhere. There will be modernisation,” he said. “They liberalised electricity. If you have money today, you can create electricity in your home. You can create it in your city. You can create it around you,” he said. Comparing the policy with the restrictions under previous military administrations, Akande said individuals were previously prevented from generating electricity independently. “Unlike what the military did before, if you tried to create electricity, they would arrest you. They would make you a debtor. They wouldn’t let you do it. They said only the Federal Government could do it. Tinubu came and said everybody can do it,” he added. On his own public engagements, the former governor attributed his reduced movement around the country to age, contrasting his present situation with when he was younger. item.title: Low voter turnout mars INEC mock election in Bayelsa, as accreditation process runs smoothly
item.description: •Reports across the state indicate a seamless exercise despite poor participation By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa The mock election organised by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) recorded a low voter turnout across Yenagoa, the Bayelsa State capital, on Saturday, despite reports of a smooth accreditation process. The exercise, designed to test the commission’s preparedness and assess the performance of its electoral technology ahead of the 2027 general elections, was seamless at the polling units visited. At the Kpansia Epie Community Town Hall, no fewer than nine voters had completed the accreditation process as of 11:15 a.m. when this reporter left the unit. The Assistant Presiding Officer, Sampson Wale, confirmed that operations with the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) were seamless. The story is not different at Epie II CPS Opolo II and others. The BVAS is being tested as part of efforts to identify and address possible challenges before the general elections. Though participation was relatively low, INEC officials expressed optimism that voter turnout would improve as the exercise progressed. Reports from other parts of the state also described the mock exercise as smooth. item.title: PHOTOS: Low Turnout as INEC begins Mock Election
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) commenced its mock elections in Borno State to test-run voting equipment and logistical readiness ahead of the 2027 general elections. However, the exercise recorded a low voter turnout in some polling units visited by our correspondent due to what many residents described as “a lack of awareness”. The exercise, designed to evaluate the deployment of election personnel and the functionality of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) across all 27 local government areas of the state, also faced a slow start in some polling units. Across Jere and Maiduguri Metropolitan Councils security personnel, including police officers and the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) and Road Safety Officials, were present early at some polling units, INEC officials arrived late. At the Bulama Jidda polling unit in Gomari Airport, voting commenced at 8:44 a.m. after officials arrived, slightly behind schedule. However, poll workers and voters at the station confirmed that the BVAS machines functioned efficiently. “There is actually a low turnout, but the use of BVAS is smooth. At some point, we are using it offline, but will upload it when we reach areas with a robust network,” one polling unit officer stated. Interviews with residents across various areas revealed that public awareness of the exercise was generally poor, with many locals unaware that the mock election was taking place. At the Gwange III polling unit, turnout was similarly low. Some prospective voters said they encountered some technical hitches during accreditation, reporting that the BVAS failed to capture their fingerprints and facial features. Speaking on condition of anonymity, an Ad-hoc staff, noted that affected individuals were not issued ballot papers. Instead, their details were compiled for INEC to review and resolve prior to the general elections. At the Government House polling unit (Unit 001, Maisandari Ward), where voter turnout was notably impressive, the process ran without hitches. Abacha Anas, the Electoral Officer for Operations for INEC in the Maiduguri Metropolitan Council, described the exercise as smooth and successful.

item.title: Gunmen kill 51-year-old man, two others in fresh Plateau attack
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa, Jos Gunmen have killed three persons in a fresh attack on Nkiedowro community in Teegbe District of Bassa Local Government Area of Plateau State, throwing residents into mourning. The attack, which occurred on Friday night, claimed the lives of three Irigwe natives, bringing to 20 the number of Irigwe people reportedly killed within the week, according to the National Publicity Secretary of the Irigwe Youth Movement, Joseph Chudu Yonkpa. Yonkpa, who confirmed the killings in a statement made available to newsmen on Saturday, said the attackers launched two separate ambushes on the community. “Yesterday night, Fulani militias launched two separate ambushes at Nkiedowro, Teegbe District, killing three Irigwe natives,” he said. He identified the victims as Ngudo Kura, 51; Hosea Ishaya, 26; and Naomi Izeh, 22. “This makes it a total of 20 Irigwe people killed this week in an unprovoked manner,” Yonkpa added. He expressed condolences to the families of the victims and the entire Irigwe community, praying for the repose of the souls of the deceased. Our correspondent reports that the latest killings occurred barely two days after 17 persons were given a mass burial following an attack on the Tafi Gana community, also in Bassa Local Government Area. The development has heightened concerns over the security situation in the area, with residents reportedly apprehensive about possible further attacks. The Irigwe Youth Movement urged residents to remain vigilant and avoid movements that could expose them to danger. “We call on our people to intensify vigilance, avoid late-night and isolated movements, and report suspicious movements to the relevant authorities,” Yonkpa said. The group also appealed to security agencies to strengthen surveillance and take necessary measures to protect communities in the area. Efforts to get the reaction of security operatives were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report. item.title: INEC Declares Readiness For 2027, Expresses Satisfaction With Plateau Mock Election
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has declared its readiness for the 2027 general elections, assuring Nigerians that it is committed to conducting free, inclusive, credible and transparent polls. INEC Chairman, Professor Joash Amupitan, gave the assurance while monitoring Saturday’s mock election in Plateau State, where he expressed satisfaction with the turnout of voters and the conduct of the exercise. Amupitan said the mock election was designed to test the functionality of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV), as well as assess the efficiency of the accreditation process ahead of the 2027 general elections. INEC Chairman Amupitan inspecting the exercise in Jos on Saturday, November 28, 2026. He commended voters for their orderly conduct, expressing delight at seeing an elderly woman turn out for the exercise and successfully undergo accreditation. “You can see yourself that the turnout is very good. What we are trying to test is actually the working of the machines, which are the BVAS and the IReV, and voters are being accredited. You can see how orderly it is going. From what we have seen, I am impressed,” he said. The INEC chairman acknowledged the support of the Plateau State Independent Electoral Commission in mobilising residents for the exercise but noted that the environmental sanitation exercise earlier scheduled for Saturday may have affected early participation, as some residents had indicated they would be unable to come out in time. On the commission’s preparedness for the 2027 elections, Amupitan said INEC was determined to deliver one of the best elections in the country’s history. “For the 2027 general elections, INEC is prepared, and I want to assure all Nigerians that we are going to have one of the best elections. We are determined that the 2027 election will be free, inclusive, credible and transparent,” he stated. Addressing concerns over the security situation in the country, the INEC chairman said the commission was working with relevant security agencies to ensure the protection of voters and electoral personnel during the forthcoming elections. He disclosed that INEC recently convened a one-day national security conference where stakeholders deliberated on security challenges and measures to safeguard the electoral process. INEC Chairman, Joash Amupitan, seen addressing staff and voters in Jos on Saturday, NOVEMBER 28, 2026. Amupitan further revealed that the commission had conducted a risk assessment of polling units across the country, with identified locations shared with law enforcement agencies to enable them to strengthen security arrangements ahead of the elections. “We have done what we call a risk assessment of all the polling units in Nigeria, and we have identified all the polling units and shared them with the law enforcement agencies so that they can make extra preparations ahead of the elections,” he said. item.title: Numbers ‘Impressive’ As Voters Turnout For INEC Mock Exercise In Kano
item.description: The mock accreditation for the 2027 general elections is underway in Paniso ward, Kano, as voters were seen turning out in seemingly impressive numbers for the exercise, compared to other regions in the country. Our correspondent, who monitored one of the selected polling units, noted that two INEC staff and two ad hoc personnel are testing the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) devices. Although voter turnout is still relatively low as against what is expected, the exercise is progressing smoothly, with no discrepancies reported and the BVAS thumbprint verification functioning as expected so far. Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Joash Amupitan, is currently in Jos to inspect the ongoing mock accreditation exercise, ahead of the 2027 general elections. It’s about seven weeks before the 2027 general election, and INEC is today running a nationwide mock accreditation and result transmission exercise in all 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). Professor Joash Amupitan, INEC Chairman, disclosed this at the INEC and Office of the National Security Adviser ONSA) Strategic Election Security Conference in Abuja on Thursday. According to him, the exercise would put the Commission’s new equipment and result systems under live conditions. “While this exercise allows INEC to stress-test our upgraded BVAS devices and verify our stricter INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV) validation safeguards—which automatically block arithmetic inconsistencies and over-voting, it also serves as an essential live dry run for our security architecture,” he said. The presidential and National Assembly elections hold on 16 January 2027 across 177,299 polling units, with governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections to follow on 6 February 2027. item.title: Kano varsity bans students, lecturers from exchanging gifts
item.description: Northwest University, Kano, has prohibited students and lecturers from giving or receiving gifts in connection with university services, warning that anyone who violates the directive will face disciplinary action. The university classified the practice as corruption and serious misconduct, stressing that the ban applies to both staff and students, irrespective of the intentions behind the gifts. The Registrar, Isyaku Adamu, announced the directive in a statement issued on Friday, following public attention generated by reports of students presenting gifts to lecturers recognised as the best level coordinators or lecturers in their respective categories. According to the registrar, the practice could damage the institution’s reputation and violate provisions of its Service Conditions and Regulations (2025), as amended. The university specifically identified the giving and receiving of gifts as acts of corruption and conduct capable of bringing the institution into disrepute. “Consequently, any staff or students found involved in giving and/or receiving gift items for university services rendered will be charged with committing an act(s) of serious misconduct and the university will immediately initiate disciplinary process against the staff or students according to the university’s regulations,” Adamu said. He added that offenders would be liable to sanctions under Section 16 of the regulations. The registrar consequently urged members of the university community to observe the institution’s rules, ethical standards and best practices to avoid disciplinary action. He also called on staff and students to take the directive seriously, adding, “A stitch in time saves nine!” Northwest University, Kano, is a state-owned institution established by the Kano State Government in 2012. It was renamed Yusuf Maitama Sule University in 2017 before reverting to its original name in 2024 following an amendment to the state law establishing it. item.title: UEFA begins probe into Marseille, Besiktas fans clash
item.description: UEFA has opened disciplinary investigations into violent incidents involving supporters of Marseille and Besiktas during their respective Europa League fixtures on Thursday. The European football governing body announced the probes on Friday, following clashes between Marseille and Levski Sofia supporters in France and a confrontation between Besiktas fans and police in Georgia. In Marseille, several hundred home supporters confronted visiting Levski Sofia fans, leaving five Bulgarian supporters hospitalised. French magistrates have also launched an investigation into alleged intentional violence involving some Marseille supporters. Authorities are equally examining allegations of incitement to hatred following claims of Nazi salutes and provocations by Bulgarian fans. Meanwhile, Besiktas’ encounter with Israeli side Hapoel Beer-Sheva in Batumi, Georgia, was temporarily halted after clashes broke out between supporters and police. The incident followed the display of a pro-Palestinian banner bearing the inscription, “Revolt against the occupation, freedom for Palestine”, alongside Palestinian flags and chants against Israel. UEFA said the incidents contradicted its commitment to ensuring that football matches are played in an atmosphere of peace, mutual respect and sporting fairness. “The events witnessed at the above-mentioned matches run counter… to UEFA’s objective, enshrined in its Statutes, of ensuring that football matches are played in a spirit of peace, mutual respect and sporting fairness,” the governing body said. It added that it had appointed Ethics and Disciplinary Inspectors to investigate the incidents. The Besiktas fixture was moved from Istanbul to Georgia after Turkish authorities informed UEFA that the match could not be hosted in Turkey for safety and security reasons. The relocation came amid worsening diplomatic relations between Turkey and Israel following the outbreak of the Gaza war. item.title: Security, INEC’s Presence Seen As Voters Trickle To Polling Units In Imo
item.description: Despite the presence of security officers and staff members of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), seen at Polling 08013 Azuzi 4 Uzi Primary School, with registered voters of 803, no single voter for mock accreditation is yet to be seen as of 11:40 am. Onuoha Onyewuchi at Azuzi Ward 4, Uzi Primary School. Onuoha Onyewuchi at Azuzi Ward 4, Uzi Primary School complained of discrepancies in the polling units. “Actually, some of us here, our various polling units; I don’t think they have been able to bring it down here. What they told us here is that there are 001-013. Some of us, 008, 005, in fact, numerous units are not here. “So, it’s only these two people that are here with me. We are still waiting for them.” Some women were also seen loitering and unable to get accredited. While briefing the media, Professor Joash Amupitan, INEC Chairman, at the INEC and Office of the National Security Adviser ONSA) Strategic Election Security Conference in Abuja on Thursday, said the exercise would put the Commission’s new equipment and result systems under live conditions. “While this exercise allows INEC to stress-test our upgraded BVAS devices and verify our stricter INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV) validation safeguards—which automatically block arithmetic inconsistencies and over-voting- it also serves as an essential live dry run for our security architecture,” he said. Ihetiobi Christian Uche, the INEC Assistant Electoral Officer, Operations, Ngorokpala LGA, speaking to Channels Television on the Mock accreditation election at Umuowa Ward 6 polling unit 006, Ngorokpala LGA, said officials arrived since 8:30 am, but no one has come for accreditation. According to him, people come only to make inquiries about PVC collection, alleging that INEC did not carry out enough sensitisation. item.title: 2027: SDP candidate promises N200 petrol, free healthcare
item.description: The presidential candidate of the Social Democratic Party (SDP), Dr Adewole Adebayo, has promised to reduce petrol prices to N200 per litre without subsidy and provide free healthcare if elected president in 2027. He also pledged free and compulsory education, increased food production, job creation and improved welfare for persons living with disabilities. Adebayo made the promises at an SDP town hall meeting with party leaders, candidates and supporters in Nasarawa State. He urged Nigerians to use the 2027 general election to determine the country’s leadership through the ballot, stressing the importance of electoral participation. Adebayo said the SDP had developed policy proposals to address poverty, unemployment, high living costs and other economic challenges facing the country. On fuel pricing, he said an SDP-led government would reduce petrol prices to N200 per litre without subsidy through improved efficiency and measures to address corruption in the petroleum sector. “We will give you petrol for N200 per litre without subsidy. We will sell it for N200, and NNPC will still make a profit because we will stop funding corruption,” he said. On agriculture, Adebayo said Nasarawa and neighbouring states had the potential to contribute significantly to national food production. “Nasarawa alone can feed Nigeria. Nasarawa, Plateau, Kogi, Kaduna and the Federal Capital Territory have the capacity to feed the whole of Africa,” he said. He also promised free and compulsory education, including measures to expand access to schooling for out-of-school children. According to him, an SDP administration would integrate children in the Almajiri system into formal education while ensuring they continued to receive religious instruction. On healthcare, Adebayo proposed establishing a Federal Medical Centre in every federal constituency and introducing compulsory medical check-ups four times annually. He also promised free medical consultations and medication, although he did not provide details of the proposed funding arrangements. On employment, the SDP candidate pledged to create more job opportunities, including for individuals living with disabilities. He also promised to develop Nasarawa’s mineral resources, including gold, coal, lithium and copper, to promote economic growth and improve the welfare of host communities. Adebayo endorsed the SDP governorship candidate in the state, former Inspector-General of Police, Abubakar Adamu, saying his experience in policing would be an asset in addressing security challenges. He urged voters to assess political candidates based on their records, character and policy proposals rather than party affiliations. The presidential candidate also called for an enabling environment for opposition parties to participate in the electoral process, stressing the importance of political competition in a democracy. item.title: Slow Turnout At Kaduna Polling Unit As INEC Holds Mock Accreditation
item.description: There is a slow turnout at polling units 031 and 032 in Ungwan Boro, Sabon Tasha ward, in Chikun Local Government Area of Kaduna State, as there is little to suggest that the mock accreditation exercise set to hold today by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) is taking place. As at the time of filing this report, at exactly 9:29 am , officials of the Independent National Electoral Commission were yet to be on ground to commence the exercise scheduled to commence by 8:3am. The only security presence observed is that of three personnel of the Nigeria Security CIVIL Defence Corps (NSCDC) There is also no presence of voters at the two polling units, raising questions about the level of preparedness and awareness ahead of the exercise. The situation contrasts with INEC’s earlier assurance of readiness for the mock election, which is designed to assess its operational capacity and the effectiveness of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System and result transmission technology ahead of the 2027 general elections. As at Friday night, when voting materials were distributed at the INEC office in Kaduna, the Administrative Secretary, Abba Yahaya, also assured the public of the Commission’s readiness for the mock election, expressing confidence in its preparedness to conduct the exercise. The exercise is expected to simulate the 2027 Presidential election, with polling units opening by 8:30 a.m. and accreditation running from 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. The situation is, however, slightly different at polling unit 002, located within Narayi Primary School, also in Chikun Local Government Area. As of 10 a.m., some voters were seen hanging around the polling area, awaiting the commencement of the exercise. However, as at the time of this report, INEC officials were yet to arrive, leaving the voters waiting without any indication of when the mock election would begin. item.title: CHINA DIARIES: Where Students Build the Future
item.description: I must confess, I was not quite prepared for what I saw during my visit to the Qinling Workshop at Xi’an Aeronautical Vocational and Technical College in China. For someone fascinated by technology and innovation, walking into the institution’s aircraft hangar was an experience in itself. There were aircraft and helicopters, aviation equipment and specialised training facilities. For a moment, it felt less like visiting a school and more like stepping into an aviation engineering centre. But the biggest surprise was yet to come. Beyond the aircraft and helicopters, I encountered something that left an even stronger impression: drones designed, developed and assembled by students. China Diaries: The Railway Connecting Continents China Diaries: The future of farming These were not simply classroom models or academic projects put together to earn grades. The students were experimenting with different drone technologies, exploring their applications and developing solutions to practical problems. There were different designs and innovations, reflecting the creativity, technical confidence and curiosity of young people who were not waiting until graduation to start making a contribution to society. It was exciting to see. One could immediately imagine the possibilities: drones that could help farmers monitor crops and spray farmlands, support environmental monitoring, conduct aerial surveys, inspect infrastructure and assist emergency response operations. What struck me most was the philosophy behind what I was seeing. Technology was not being taught as an abstract subject. Students were being encouraged to understand problems and develop technological solutions. An institution built around practical skills The Qinling Workshop visit offered an opportunity to appreciate the work of Xi’an Aeronautical Vocational and Technical College, an institution with a strong focus on aviation, engineering and technical education. Its programmes cover a wide range of disciplines, including aviation manufacturing, aircraft maintenance, aircraft engine technology, drone application technology, general aviation, mechanical engineering, artificial intelligence, computer technology, robotics, automation, electronic information, aviation logistics and automotive technology. Students also study specialised areas such as CNC machining, intelligent manufacturing, aircraft electronic systems, materials engineering, welding technology, surveying and remote sensing, software development, big data, airport operations and civil aviation services. The breadth of these programmes is significant. It shows an understanding that an aviation and manufacturing economy requires much more than pilots and aircraft engineers. It needs technicians, software developers, mechanics, materials specialists, electronics experts, maintenance professionals and people who can design, manufacture and repair equipment.
